instructions: Season the wings with the salt and 1/4 tsp of the pepper. Toss to coat and put them in the fridge.
Grate the ginger and squeeze out 1 tsp of juice. Grate the garlic clove.

In a small saucepan over medium-high heat, simmer the sugar, soy sauce, sake, ginger juice and garlic until the glaze thickens and the bubbles turn large and glossy, about 8 minutes. Stir in the vinegar and transfer the glaze to a large bowl.
Pour the oil into a heavy pot, about 2 inches deep, and heat it to 320°F. If you have no thermometer, a wooden chopstick put in the oil should give off a slow, steady stream of small bubbles.
Pat the wings very dry. Dust them with the potato starch in a thin, even layer and shake off the extra.
Fry the wings in batches for about 10 minutes, until they're pale golden and cooked through. Transfer them to a rack as they come out.
Raise the oil to 375°F. Fry the wings again in small batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're deep golden and very crisp.
Transfer the hot wings to the bowl of glaze and toss to coat. Sprinkle with the sesame seeds and the last 1/4 tsp pepper.
method_notes: The lead and the other versions agree on the Nagoya way: a very light dusting of potato starch and two fries, a gentle one to cook the wings through and a hot one to crisp them. Glaze is sugar, soy sauce and sake cooked down with ginger and garlic, with a lot of black pepper at the end. Other versions glaze with mirin and honey; this follows the lead. Frying takes a thermometer or a steady eye on the oil.
